ARCHITECTURE NOTE: this solver trains ONLY a handful of nn.Parameter scalars (per-band log-scale x4, sigmoid slope+offset x2, per-outer soft-threshold + residual-blend) wrapped around a band-weighted aliasing-free FBP + a soft-thresholded dense-residual pass; with wu_n_outer=1 that is 4+2+1+1 = 8 trainable scalars (n_bands=4). CONFIG: wu_n_outer=1 (the discarded boundary-slice run flagged n_outer=1 as mandatory -- behavior hint only; it also HALVES the costly 2x-dense-projector residual pass per sample, the dominant per-slice cost), wu_n_bands=4 (default), lr=1e-2 (solver default; aggressive lr is fine for ~8 scalars and converges fast), epochs=6 (8 clamped scalars settle in very few epochs at lr=1e-2 -- this is NOT a deep net that under-trains; the real risk here is the opposite structural FBP ceiling, not under-convergence), train_n=200 stratified across the 4 Wagner train patients ps-groups, val_n=214 = ALL L277 slices, batch_size=1 + val_chunk=1 FORCED by per-sample-ps (each train step + each val slice swaps model.proj AND model.dense_proj to its slice ps), grad_clip=1.0 (MANDATORY Mayo guard: the 2304-view FBP adjoint overflows otherwise), lambda_neg=1.0, weight_decay=0.0 (defer to iter-2+; the discarded run hinted weight_decay tuning around its run-best iter-11, treat as loose behavior hint only), loss_base=mse, seed=42. BUDGET REASONING: the solver has NO in-code max_train_s wall hook (cannot add one -- must not edit the solver .py), so the budget is enforced by SIZING: with wu_n_outer=1 the per-sample cost is 1 band-weighted sparse-FBP (4-band backproject) + 1 forward_project + 1 dense-FBP + 1 back_project -- heavier than DD-UNet (iter-1 418s @ep8) but LIGHTER than the unrolled k=3 itnet_v3 (iter-1 738s @ep8) because there is no per-step unrolled DC loop; at only 6 epochs over 200 train slices the dominant cost is the 214-slice val pass at chunk=1 with the dense projector. This sizes train+score comfortably under the 20-min budget (30-min SLURM wall) with room for the figure. HYPOTHESIS: if I fit Wu-trainable at n_outer=1 / lr=1e-2 / ep=6 on 200 stratified Mayo train slices, I expect a finite val_ssim that lands in/near the LD-FBP baseline band (~0.84-0.89 SSIM, hr near 0), because Wu-trainable is a tuned-FBP family (band-reweighting + ONE soft-thresholded residual pass, NO image-domain CNN denoiser) and can only recover the small headroom that band weighting + a single residual correction buys over plain FBP -- it is structurally close to FBP, unlike the dual-domain U-Net families that landed hr~0.27. The discarded boundary-slice run hinted ~0.9135 SSIM at run-best iter-11 (loose behavior hint, NOT a validated number under the corrected 214-slice 321px-FOV metric). This onboarding iter establishes the corrected-metric Wu-trainable baseline that iter-2+ will improve by tuning ONE knob (epochs/weight_decay first, then band/sigmoid knobs).
